page.running_head: SECT. I. PART. I. CAP. XI.

main_text.p: do, calorem corrumpendo, omnemque rarefactio-nem & attenuationem impediendo: flupefacit & ad motum inepta reddit animalia, calorem, qui motus instrumentum est, interimendo, mollesque ac fle-xiles corporum partes constringendo: Exiccat, hu-morem exprimendo vel condensando: poros occludit, vaporem calidum ex imis corporibus expirantem, condensando & constringendo: cruditates generat, concoctionem impediendo, & ascendentes ad caput vapores in pituitam, quae, instar pluviae, per nares destillat, condensando: Zanardus hasce frigoris actio-nes recensent: Frigiditas est, 1. a circumferentia ad centrum motiva. 2. Accidentaliter calefactiva. 3. con-densativa. 4. per accidens diffolutiva & partium disjun-ctiva. 5. naturaliter ingroffativa. 6. partium ignis in ac-rem condensativa. 7. accidentaliter subtilitativa. 8. ac-cidentaliter alleviativa. 9. si temperata sit, vitae rei con-servativa. 10. accidentaliter corruptiva & destructiva. 11. naturaliter discolorativa. 12. accidentaliter colorativa. 13. Si intensa sit, mortificativa. 14. accidentaliter vivifi-cativa. 15. albificativa. 16. objecti sui & virtutis manifefta-tiva.
II. Coronidis vice nonnullas de frigore quae-stiunculas proponemus & discutiemus.
Sit igitur prima quaestio: Sitne frigus qualitas priva-tiva, an positiva?

Privationem esse non tantum Aristoteles affirmat, lib. 1. de generat. & corrupt. cap. 3. text. 18, & lib. 2. de Coelo, cap. 3. text. 18. & 12. metaphys. cap. 4. text. 12. & lib. 2. de ortu animalium cap. 4. Denique 1. Metaphys. cap. 4. Sed & ratione videtur suaderi posse.

page.notes: The scan is slightly skewed at the right edge. The page number is printed as "49ȝ" (the 3 is an old form), so I read it as 493 with a doubt marked. The question "Sitne" may carry an accent over the e, and I have copied it as printed. The centred word "Nam" at the foot is the catchword. The left strip is the edge of the facing page and is excluded.
